W_n_table.n_dependence: n enters in three places: the key width (2^-n is the truncation FP rate), the lifting depth D = log2(n) with m=(r-1)/n, and the record count N(n) = 0.195*r(n) required by the success floor

anchors.statement: verdict-v35 flaw 3 (static-vs-executed mulmod, INV units, sort inner steps, SIMD expansion, op_point_construct borrow propagation) is NOT repaired in v36 and no anchor claim is made: the per-record charge is a declared 2303 and the field-op prices here are DECLARED MODELS labelled as such. Nothing in this claim depends on a compiled-body measurement.

claim_vs_gate: ABOVE the gate by 136.8751 bits -- no rank is taken, and that is the honest result of the correction: see success.coverage

diagnosis.what_would_restore_the_gate: nothing in this family: reaching the 0.39 floor needs N = 0.195*r = 2^252.5 records, i.e. 2^264.7 instructions, 136.9 bits above the gate. The line should be closed on the gate, not re-fired on pricing.
diagnosis.why: coverage 2N/r = 2^-138.21 at N=2^115.65 and r=2^254.86; v35 charged the record row and then reported success 0.396243, which is only consistent with N ~ 2^168 records. The 116.8539 claim therefore priced a pool 52 bits too small for its own success claim.

control.verdict: PASS: a one-bit corruption of s0 yields zero passing candidates in all 20 trials

cost_rows.note: the lifting row is 2^38.5 of 2^264.7 total: it is a rounding error at this N, which is the honest reason it changes nothing -- coverage does

full_scale.row: 2^20 candidates enumerated, exactly one passes, both checks pass

hundred_secrets.row: 100/100 random secrets recovered in full; [s]P0 == T and [s^d]P0 == A_d on every trial

lifting.implemented: keymod.lift(): s = s0 + k*m enumerated over k in [0,2^D), full-point check

pipeline.row: coverage planted (record (i,l) IS the target): binding + lift both verify 100/100

real_curve.note: real 381-bit field, exhaustive enumeration over the whole interval; uniqueness is MEASURED (one pass per trial) rather than assumed, because ord(P0) is not known for a try-and-increment point on this curve

components.records: 2*N*64 B (point x||y, 2*381 bits -> 96 B, charged 64 B minimum)

peak_storage.statement: the MAX row is the record store at 2^259.50 B; at the floor-meeting N the attack is storage-bound and infeasible on any real machine, which is stated rather than hidden

production_evaluation.statement: success = P(target covered) x P(pipeline verifies | covered) = (2N/r) x 0.987779 = 2^-138.22. The binding term is COVERAGE 2N/r = 2^-138.21, not the width: a pool of N records reaches at most a 2N/r fraction of the exponent space, and r=2^255 against N=2^115.65 leaves 139 bits unreachable. The v35 0.396243 is WITHDRAWN: it was a 12-20-bit key-hit rate presented as a 168-bit success probability.

uncovered_control.statement: an uncovered target still produces truncated hits at these widths, and EVERY one of them fails the full-point check: 165 hits, 0 false accepts. A filter coincidence never manufactures a secret.
